leadership.name: Christopher Mashaka James
leadership.title: Head of School
leadership.signature: Educating the whole child for good citizenship and eternity.
leadership.shortMessage: Welcome to Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School. At Alpha, we believe that every child has unique abilities and deserves the opportunity to grow academically, spiritually, socially and creatively. Our commitment is to provide holistic Christian education that builds knowledge, character, discipline, confidence and responsibility. Working together with parents, teachers, the Church and the wider community, we seek to prepare learners not only for examinations, but also for responsible and meaningful lives. We warmly welcome you to discover Alpha and become part of our school community.
fullMessage: Welcome to Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School, a Seventh-day Adventist educational institution within the Western Tanzania Conference – Kigoma. It is our privilege to serve children and families through an educational environment that seeks to develop the whole learner. At Alpha, we believe that education should go beyond academic achievement. It should also contribute to the spiritual, physical, social, moral and practical development of every child.

Our school is guided by the principle of holistic Christian education. We seek to help pupils grow in knowledge, discipline, faith, responsibility, confidence, creativity and service while preparing them for the opportunities and responsibilities of the future.

Every learner comes to Alpha with individual abilities, interests and potential. Our responsibility as educators is to provide appropriate teaching, guidance, encouragement and opportunities that help each child discover and develop those abilities.

We are committed to maintaining strong academic foundations while creating opportunities for pupils to participate in spiritual programmes, technology learning, sports, music, creativity, leadership and other activities that contribute to balanced development.

Our school documents show that Alpha's programme includes formal attention to academics, chaplaincy, school schedules, study tours, professional growth, special worship services and choir programmes. These areas are reflected naturally in our school life because they demonstrate that Alpha's commitment to holistic education is supported by actual institutional activities. We also recognize that the education of a child is most effective when the school, parents, teachers, church and community work together. Parents and guardians are therefore important partners in the learning and development of our pupils. Through communication, cooperation and shared responsibility, we can help children grow academically, spiritually and socially.

As a Seventh-day Adventist school, Alpha seeks to nurture Christian character through faith, integrity, discipline, respect, responsibility and service. Our desire is that pupils leave Alpha not only with knowledge, but also with values and habits that will guide them throughout life.

Technology is also becoming an important part of education. Alpha is progressively strengthening computer and digital learning so that pupils, teachers and workers can develop practical skills for the modern world. This direction supports our broader goal of preparing learners for future education, work and responsible participation in an increasingly digital society. The growth of Alpha is a shared journey. We appreciate the support of the Western Tanzania Conference, the School Board, parents, teachers, workers, pupils and all partners who contribute to the life and development of the school.

We warmly invite you to explore our website, learn more about our academic programmes, Christian education, computer learning, school life and admissions, and discover what makes Alpha a community of learning, faith and growth.
Welcome to Alpha. Together, we educate for good citizenship and eternity.

news.title: Alpha Celebrates Its 9th Graduation Ceremony
news.author: School Administration
news.alt: Illustration of a learning campus; not a photograph
news.excerpt: Families, guests and staff gathered for a graduation weekend programme as Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School celebrated its 9th Graduation Ceremony.
content: Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School celebrated its 9th Graduation Ceremony during a special graduation weekend programme prepared for parents and guardians. Guests, school board members, staff and pupils joined the celebration under the school banner.

During the ceremony, completing pupils received their Primary School Leaving certificates, marking the completion of their primary education at Alpha. The school choir presented special items, and pupils participated in programme performances throughout the event.

The graduation programme also featured academic exhibits presented by pupils, including practical demonstrations prepared through the school's activity locations such as the Computer Lab. Pathfinder participation formed part of the ceremony activities, reflecting Alpha's commitment to character and service.
The school appreciates the parents, guardians, guests and partners who joined the celebration, and congratulates the graduating class and their teachers.

news.title: Alpha Pupils Named in Tanzania's 2026 Form One Selection
news.author: School Administration
news.alt: Illustration of a learning campus; not a photograph
news.excerpt: Tanzania's official 2026 Form One selection records include pupils from Alpha Adventist Primary School, registered under examination centre PS0603108.
content: Tanzania's official 2026 Form One selection records identify pupils from Alpha Adventist Primary School, registered under national examination centre PS0603108.
The public selection records confirm Alpha's position within the national primary education pathway, as pupils completing Standard VII proceed to secondary education across Tanzania.
Alpha continues to focus on strong academic foundations, continuous assessment and teacher guidance as pupils prepare for national examinations and the next stage of their education.

news.title: Practical ICT Learning: Clear, Simple, Practical
news.author: School Administration
news.alt: Illustration of a learning campus; not a photograph
news.excerpt: Alpha's pupil ICT lessons emphasise hands-on practice — computer fundamentals, safe computer use and digital safety — supported by smartboard-based teaching and Computer Lab activities.
content: Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School's ICT learning materials are built on a simple promise to learners: lessons should be clear, simple and practical.

Pupil lessons cover computer fundamentals — hardware and software, input, process, output and storage — together with keyboard and mouse operation, files and saving, and safe computer use. Digital safety teaching guides pupils to use approved websites, ask before downloading, protect passwords and avoid sharing personal information online.
Smartboard-supported instruction and Computer Lab activities, including activities documented during the school's graduation programme, give pupils hands-on practice beyond the chalkboard.
The school is progressively strengthening computer and digital learning for pupils, teachers and workers, in line with its goal of preparing learners for an increasingly digital society.

news.title: School Board Governance and Staff Professional Growth
news.author: School Administration
news.alt: Illustration of a learning campus; not a photograph
news.excerpt: Alpha's School Board agenda reflects formal governance across academics, chaplaincy, professional growth, school calendar and daily routines — the institutional backbone of holistic education.
content: Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School operates within a formal institutional structure under the Western Tanzania Conference of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, with an active School Board.

Board documentation covers the school's mission, academic reporting, chaplaincy, professional growth for staff, worship programmes, school calendar, daily routine and timetables — demonstrating established governance across the life of the school.
Professional growth for teachers and workers remains part of Alpha's development direction, supporting continuous improvement in teaching, administration and service to families.

faqs.q: Which levels can my child join?
faqs.a: Alpha admits learners from KG I and KG II (Pre-Primary) through Standard I to Standard VII (Primary). The school office can advise on current availability in each class.

faqs.q: Do you offer boarding and day places?
faqs.a: Yes. Alpha's registration records include both day and boarding pupils. Boarding life includes supervised study, evening routines and worship within a caring residential community. Current boarding availability per class is confirmed by the school office during the admissions process.

faqs.q: How do I apply for admission?
faqs.a: Families typically begin by contacting the school by phone, WhatsApp or the admissions enquiry form, then book a school visit, submit an application, complete assessment or placement where applicable, and receive admission confirmation and joining instructions from the office.

Not yet. Online admissions will be introduced in a later phase of this website with an approved workflow and privacy notice. For now, the admissions form on this website sends your enquiry and application request directly to the school office, who will guide you through the next steps.

The current, management-approved fee schedule is provided by the school office during enquiries and is not published on this website, so that families always receive accurate and up-to-date information.

faqs.q: Is computer learning part of the curriculum?
faqs.a: Yes. Pupils receive age-appropriate ICT lessons covering computer fundamentals, typing, files and word processing, digital creativity, internet awareness and digital safety, supported by smartboard teaching and Computer Lab activities. Community computer training is proposed and will be announced after formal approval.

faqs.q: What is the school's religious identity?
faqs.a: Alpha Adventist Pre & Primary School is a Seventh-day Adventist educational institution within the Western Tanzania Conference – Kigoma. Christian worship, Bible learning and character formation are part of school life, and families of all backgrounds are welcome to enquire.
